title: Sulking with the Heart
note: She sulks with her heart, which longs for union and won’t think of sulking even when there is cause, and he does the same with his. That also explains the chapter’s place here.

couplets.plain: You see how his heart stands by him. Why, heart, won’t you stand by me?
couplets.pm: Heart, you have seen that his heart doesn’t think of us and stands by him. Why won’t you stand by me, instead of thinking of him? Standing by me here means agreeing to sulk. People who can’t work out a task for themselves will do it by watching someone else, and you won’t do even that.
couplets.context: He is at fault, yet her heart won’t think of sulking. She says this to it.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: Even when you see he isn’t drawn to us, my heart, you go to him, sure he won’t be angry.
couplets.pm: My heart, even when you know for certain that he has no loving-kindness for us, you go to him, sure that he won’t be angry if we come. Can there be greater ignorance? You rely on his old regard to keep him from anger. Will that get you what you want?
couplets.context: She goes on, to her heart.
couplets.speaker: she

links.reason: Accuses her heart of going to the man who isn’t drawn to her.

couplets.plain: Is it because the ruined have no friends, heart, that you go after him as you please?
couplets.pm: Heart, you don’t stay with me but go to him as you wish. Is it that you think the ruined have no friends in this world, or is it your nature? Tell me. She says “as you please” because leaving her is its old habit, and “ruined” because she now has no pride. Your bond, she says, is like that of the senseless, who fall away when you fail.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her heart.
couplets.speaker: she

links.reason: Charges her heart with deserting her, as friends desert the ruined.

couplets.plain: You won’t sulk first and enjoy him after. So who will plan such things with you from now on, heart?
couplets.pm: Heart, as soon as you see him you think only of enjoying him. You don’t look at his fault, start a sulk first, take its measure and enjoy him after. So who will plan such things with you now? I won’t. She meant all along to sulk, and then grew eager for union, so she says this.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her heart.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: You won’t sulk first and enjoy him after.

couplets.plain: My heart fears not having him, and when it has him it fears parting. Its suffering never ends.
couplets.pm: When it doesn’t have my lover my heart fears that, and when it has him it dwells on the parting to come and fears that. So its suffering never leaves. She is agreeing to the plea, thinking it unwise to have him and lose union. Not yet sated, she also fears he may leave again. There are only these two, so the suffering never ends.
couplets.context: Her friend comes as his go-between, and she says this for her friend to hear.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: when it has him it fears parting

couplets.plain: When I sat alone and thought, my heart stayed with me only to eat me up.
couplets.pm: When I was apart from my lover and thought over his cruelties, my heart stayed here only to torment me as if devouring me. It wasn’t on my side. It took in his cruelties to make me suffer, not so that I could sulk with him over them today.
couplets.context: She goes on, for her friend to hear.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: Caught up with this worthless, foolish heart that can’t forget him, I have forgotten even my modesty.
couplets.pm: Joined to my unworthy, foolish heart, which can’t forget the lover who forgot it, I have forgotten even modesty, worth more than my life. The heart can’t hold steady. It remembers his fault when he is away and forgets it when he is here, where it should do the reverse. Modesty is shrinking from him, however long you have been together, as if seeing him for the first time.
couplets.context: She goes on, for her friend to hear.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: Caught up with this worthless, foolish heart

couplets.plain: My heart, in love with life, thinks it would be shameful to scorn him, and so it keeps thinking of his ways.
couplets.pm: My heart, in love with life, thinks: if we scorn him for scorning us, we will be shamed later. So it thinks only of him. To scorn him is to turn away his go-between. The shame comes from failing him, from being unable to bear parting, and from losing modesty and reserve. Fearing shame and unable to die, my heart means to join him.
couplets.note: உயிர்க்காதல் could also be a love as dear as life. He takes it as love of life: the heart can’t bring itself to die.
couplets.context: She goes on, for her friend to hear.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: In trouble, who will stand by you if your own heart won’t?
couplets.pm: When trouble comes, if your own heart doesn’t help you, no one else will. The trouble here is that her sulk won’t yield to his pleading. His heart fails him by longing for union, instead of deciding she has no loving-kindness and giving her up. With no help at all, he can only bear it and let it go.
couplets.context: She is sulking and won’t be won over by his pleading, and he says this.
couplets.speaker: he

couplets.plain: If your own heart isn’t on your side, it is a small thing that strangers aren’t.
couplets.pm: If the heart you own isn’t on your side, need it be said that outsiders aren’t? My own heart takes this other woman for my beloved and torments me. After that, it is a small matter that she sulks.
couplets.context: She is still sulking, and he goes on.
couplets.speaker: he
